edges.label: minority witness
edges.note: Called by Ranking Member Crockett, who devoted her entire round to him.

b.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

edges.label: Knapp's Russian MoD documents handed to BAASS/DIA for AAWSAP analysis
edges.note: Knapp's custody allegation, made under oath: 'I have confirmed on the record that Robert Bigelow and a trusted colleague from AAWSAP met with and negotiated with senior executives at Lockheed Martin and hammered out a deal wherein Bigelow's company, BAASS, would receive a quantity of unusual material that had been stashed away and protected at a facility in California. That material was not made here.' On the Russia files he testified that he obtained documents and interviews from Soviet defence officials in the early 1990s and has 'now shared with this Task Force' - the printed hearing carries no statement that he shared them with BAASS or the DIA, which is why this is tier 2. It is an allegation by a named witness, not a documented transfer.

b.label: Harry M. Reid

edges.label: Knapp's Lazar/S-4 reporting opened a private channel to Reid
edges.note: Knapp told the Task Force that after reporting the Bob Lazar / S-4 story in 1989 he 'interviewed dozens of other people' over the years, and named the list: 'They include Senator Harry Reid; Senator Howard Cannon, also of Nevada; a guy named Al O'Donnell, who was the first general manager of EG&G in Nevada... There is a guy named Dr. James Lacatski.' The printed hearing reproduces oral statements only, so the sequence in which Knapp first approached Reid sits in his written statement at docs.house.gov and is not asserted here.

b.label: House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing, 9 September 2025 - 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection'

edges.label: Knapp testified as KLAS-TV chief investigative reporter
edges.note: Knapp opened his sworn statement: 'I am George Knapp, chief investigative reporter at KLAS-TV in Las Vegas. I began my pursuit of this weird mystery way back in 1987, and for 38 years, I have always approached this as a news story. It is not a matter of faith or belief to me.' The witness list gives him as 'Mr. George Knapp, UAP Journalist'; Chairwoman Luna's introduction dates his arrival at KLAS to 1981 and the chief investigative reporter post to 1995.

b.label: Independent media as the disclosure substrate

edges.label: four decades of the record produced from a single local affiliate
edges.note: KLAS-TV is where George Knapp has anchored and reported since 1981, where the Bob Lazar interviews aired in 1989, and the institutional capacity in which he testified before the House Oversight Task Force on 9 September 2025. A local CBS affiliate in a desert market holding a national investigative record for forty years is a structural fact about the substrate, not a curiosity.

b.label: James T. Lacatski

edges.label: Knapp co-authored two books with the AAWSAP originator
edges.note: Knapp named Lacatski on the record as one of the people he has interviewed: 'There is a guy named Dr. James Lacatski, who was a career scientist with the Defense Intelligence Agency, who was the guy who initiated a program called AAWSAP, Advanced Aerospace Weapons Systems Application Program, which is, as far as we know, the largest acknowledged UFO program ever funded by the U.S. Government.'

b.label: Air Force Plant 42, Palmdale, California

edges.label: The unnamed 'facility in California' in the sworn testimony is most plausibly in the Palmdale complex
edges.note: Reasoning: Knapp specified California and Lockheed; Lockheed's California SAP-accredited aeronautics footprint is concentrated at Palmdale. No witness has named a site and the board does not assert one.

b.label: Bigelow Aerospace

edges.label: Alleged negotiated transfer of non-terrestrial material from a Lockheed California facility to BAASS
edges.note: George Knapp testified under oath on 9 September 2025 that Robert Bigelow and an AAWSAP colleague negotiated with senior Lockheed Martin executives for material 'stashed away and protected at a facility in California' that 'was not made here.' Luis Elizondo confirmed to the House on 13 November 2024 that the transfer was blocked.

b.label: Federal Contracting Mechanics

edges.label: the prime where classified contract line items and sworn allegation meet
edges.note: Lockheed Martin's prime contract obligations run to the hundreds of billions of dollars in USAspending records, a portion carried as classified line items visible in financial systems only as a number. It is also the only company named on the floor of a congressional hearing by a sworn witness in connection with the custody allegation, which makes it the test case for whether contracting records can be made to answer the question.

b.label: Ken Klippenstein

edges.label: Member of Congress characterizes the records leak as a discrediting operation
edges.note: At the 9 September 2025 Task Force hearing Mace told a witness: 'We know they did that to Mr. Grusch. They leaked his private medical information, horrific things.' The statement is in the official record; the identity of 'they' is not.

b.label: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)

edges.label: Stated the compartmentation trap in a public hearing
edges.note: 'only certain people know the name of the program, and if you do not know it, you cannot get the information.' This is the operational definition of an unacknowledged program from the oversight side.

b.label: Anna Paulina Luna

edges.label: POGO recommendations delivered to Luna's task force
edges.note: Spielberger's testimony is addressed to 'Chairwoman Luna, Ranking Member Crockett, and task force members' and lays out a legislative agenda for protecting UAP whistleblowers. Luna convened and chaired the hearing; the connection is a witness-to-chair relationship at a single hearing, not an ongoing partnership.

edges.label: POGO counsel testified at the UAP transparency hearing
edges.note: The transcript lists 'Mr. Joe Spielberger (Minority Witness), Senior Policy Counsel, Project on Government Oversight'. His statement opens 'Chairwoman Luna, Ranking Member Crockett, and Task Force members' and describes POGO as 'a nonpartisan independent watchdog organization that investigates and exposes waste, corruption, abuse of power, and when the government fails to serve the public or silences those who report wrongdoing.' He appeared as the minority witness, on whistleblower protection rather than on the phenomenon.

b.label: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

edges.label: Outside watchdog seated as witness before Oversight's declassification task force
edges.note: The hearing's own masthead gives the forum exactly: 'HEARING BEFORE THE TASK FORCE ON THE DECLASSIFICATION OF FEDERAL SECRETS OF THE COMMITTEE ON OVERSIGHT AND GOVERNMENT REFORM'. POGO appeared through Joe Spielberger, its senior policy counsel, listed as the minority witness, and used the appearance to argue for statutory whistleblower protection rather than to make claims about the phenomenon.
